free_tier.stated: "On the European Galaxy server every user has a 250 GB quota. This means you can use 250 GB of storage for free." The storage is funded by the de.NBI cloud and the University of Freiburg compute centre, which held 4 PB of user data as of January 2025, and the page states the quota form for extra storage has been discontinued because storage "has become increasingly scarce and expensive".

interface_detail: REST API (Galaxy API), documented: the API documentation is at /api/docs or /api/redoc under the server base URL; the web interface is the other way in.
tooling: BioBlend, the Python library for the Galaxy API (also blend4php, blend4j and a TypeScript schema); the REST API directly otherwise.
chaining: Two independent Galaxy servers give two independent 250 GB quotas, because they are funded by different institutions and share no account system, so the pair composes to 500 GB of free storage for the same one email address and the same tool wrappers.

limits.value: the page states that at the limit no new jobs start.

notes: Recorded separately from Galaxy Main because the operator, the funder and the storage policy differ, and because the withdrawn quota form is a fact that applies only here. The compute behind the EU server is not quantified on the pages read, so vcpu and memory are null rather than copied from the US figures, which are TACC and Jetstream and do not describe this machine. A reader should treat 250 GB as long-term storage and note that short-term scratch storage and bring-your-own storage are offered as the route for larger jobs, which is what the page tells users to use instead of a quota increase.
